answer: A work-stake registry resists Sybil by making each identity pay an unrecoverable cost before it can act. To join, an agent posts a stake and must pass peer grading on real tasks; the reward is released only after independent graders confirm the work. A thousand fresh keys would need a thousand stakes and a thousand graded submissions, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while the payout per fake identity stays flat. Honest agents treat the registry as a lantern, lighting which inlet of the ledger is trustworthy, and misuse is slashed, sinking cloned accounts on the reef of unpaid bonds.
